title: Parallel and perpendicular lines

draft.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
card: Parallel lines have equal gradients. The lines \(y = 3x + 1\) and \(y = 3x - 4\) both have gradient 3.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Their gradients multiply to give \(-1\). For example, \(2 \times -\frac{1}{2} = -1\).
To find a perpendicular gradient, flip the fraction and change the sign. The gradient \(\frac{3}{4}\) becomes \(-\frac{4}{3}\).
Read the gradient \(m\) from the form \(y = mx + c\). For \(y = -5x + 2\), the gradient is \(-5\), so a perpendicular line has gradient \(\frac{1}{5}\).
draft.remember: Parallel: equal gradients. Perpendicular: gradients multiply to \(-1\).

a.q: A line has gradient \(\frac{2}{3}\). What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it?
a.why: Flip \(\frac{2}{3}\) to \(\frac{3}{2}\) and change the sign, giving \(-\frac{3}{2}\). Check: \(\frac{2}{3} \times -\frac{3}{2} = -1\). Only flipping, with no sign change, gives a product of 1.
a.clue: Flip the fraction and change the sign.

b.why: The gradient of \(y = 4x - 7\) is 4, so a perpendicular gradient is \(-\frac{1}{4}\), since \(4 \times -\frac{1}{4} = -1\). The line \(y = 4x + 3\) is parallel, not perpendicular.
b.clue: Find the gradient first, then flip it and change the sign.
